results.title: Plural *_ids hydration blindly calls .map on null/undefined and can drop unresolved relationship ids
distinct_defects: unguarded plural ids hydration branch in store.js.es6
results.explanation: All findings describe symptoms of the same new plural ids hydration branch lacking the guard/type checks present for singular hydration, causing either data loss or crashes.

results.title: Embeddable hosts saved with a port never match because lookup drops the port
distinct_defects: port handling mismatch between validation and lookup
missing controller test coverage for mutating endpoints and fallbacks
case-insensitive host comparison only lowercases stored column
results.explanation: The findings cover three separate root causes: a port-validation/lookup mismatch, insufficient controller spec coverage, and a case-sensitivity mismatch in host lookup.

results.title: EmbeddableHost hostname validation regex rejects valid hosts (long gTLDs, localhost/IP) and is inconsistent about ports
distinct_defects: Overly restrictive hostname/TLD validation regex
Port/path allowed in stored host but matching uses uri.host without port
Migrated legacy rows bypass validation and normalization
results.explanation: Most findings share the restrictive hostname regex root cause, but the port-matching mismatch and migration bypass are separate defects with different fixes.

results.title: EmbeddableHost allows duplicate host mappings, making lookup via `.first` nondeterministic
distinct_defects: missing case-insensitive uniqueness on EmbeddableHost.host causing nondeterministic category lookup
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: EmbeddableHost.host lacks uniqueness enforcement, so duplicate rows exist and the unordered .first lookup picks a nondeterministic category for imported topics.

results.title: EmbeddableHost persists arbitrary categoryid without verifying category exists or is accessible
distinct_defects: missing foreign key/validation/cleanup for embeddablehosts.categoryid when a category is deleted
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: embeddablehost.category_id has no foreign key, presence validation, or dependent cleanup, so deleting a category leaves dangling ids that break topicembed imports and render blank categories.

results.title: Irreversible destructive data migration in `change` permanently deletes site settings on rollback
distinct_defects: destructive data migration inside def change with no inverse down path
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the migration performs destructive, non-invertible data operations (delete from sitesettings) inside def change, so rollback drops the table while leaving the deleted settings unrecoverable.

results.title: Migration uses create_table force: true causing silent drop/recreate and data loss
distinct_defects: create_table :embeddable_hosts with force: true silently drops and recreates a pre-existing table, destroying data
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the shipped migration's `create_table ... force: true` destructively drops any pre-existing embeddablehosts table and its rows instead of failing loudly.

results.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding update is a no-op that returns 200 without persisting changes
distinct_defects: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that returns success without reading or persisting params
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the admin embedding update endpoint re-renders the serialized model without applying submitted changes, making saves silent no-ops.

results.title: Migration skips importing legacy embeddable hosts by using cmdtuples on a SELECT, then deletes the only copy of the config
distinct_defects: dead cmdtuples > 0 guard on SELECT makes backfill import never run, then delete destroys legacy hosts
results.explanation: All findings identify the same root cause: the migration guards the host import on embeddablehosts.cmdtuples > 0, which is always 0 for a SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the import is dead code and the subsequent delete silently removes configured hosts.

results.title: Routes expose REST actions for embeddable_hosts that the controller doesn't implement (ActionNotFound on GET)
distinct_defects: resources :embeddablehosts exposes unimplemented index/show/new/edit actions
results.explanation: All findings describe the same mismatch between the full RESTful routes declared for :embeddablehosts and the controller implementing only create/update/destroy, fixed by restricting routes with only: [:create, :update, :destroy].

results.title: EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids (no sideloaded embeddable_hosts), breaking client hydration
distinct_defects: EmbeddingSerializer has_many :embeddablehosts embed: :ids missing include: true, so no embeddablehosts side-load for client hydration
results.explanation: All three findings describe the same serializer configuration defect (has_many :embeddablehosts, embed: :ids without include: true) that omits side-loaded host records and breaks store.js hydration.

results.title: EmbeddableHost host format validation allows trailing newline due to end-anchor, creating broken allowlist entries
distinct_defects: Improper regex anchoring in host validation allows trailing-newline bypass
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the host-format regex permits malformed values with a trailing newline, causing allowlist bypass or stored non-matching entries.

results.title: EmbedController authorization can be bypassed by forging the Referer header
distinct_defects: Referer-header-based authorization for embed endpoints is spoofable
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same root cause: embed endpoints are authorized solely via the attacker-controllable Referer header, allowing forged requests to read embedded content.

results.title: Google Meet event creation can crash when destinationCalendar is missing/empty
distinct_defects: Missing optional chaining on mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration in EventManager Google Meet fallback
results.explanation: All findings describe the same missing null guard/optional chaining on mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration in the EventManager Google Meet fallback, causing a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty.

results.title: Reschedule calendar update errors are swallowed: catch returns [] when calendarReference is unset and logs were removed
distinct_defects: updateAllCalendarEvents catch block swallows errors and may return an empty array instead of failure result/logging
results.explanation: All findings describe the same catch-block defect in updateAllCalendarEvents: removed error logging and failure to return a failure result when the throw occurs before calendarReference is assigned.

results.title: Booking webhook payload breaks backward compatibility by changing destinationCalendar from object/null to array
distinct_defects: destinationcalendar webhook payload type changed from object/null to array
results.explanation: All findings describe the same unversioned breaking change where the destinationcalendar field in webhook payloads changed from object/null to array, with differing symptoms across producers and consumers.

results.title: Recurring cancellation delete sweep runs once per calendar reference, causing redundant deleteEvent calls (O(n) duplicates/404s)
distinct_defects: Recurring deletion sweep nested inside bookingCalendarReference loop causing duplicate provider deletes/404s
Inner references.find only deletes the first calendar reference per updated booking, leaving orphaned secondary-host events
results.explanation: All findings describe the nested-loop duplicate-delete bug, but findings 2 and 6 also identify a separate first-reference lookup defect that leaves orphaned recurring events.

results.title: eventmanager.update swallows errors and returns [] when calendarReference is undefined
distinct_defects: eventmanager.update catch returns empty array (and drops log) instead of failure result when throw precedes calendarreference assignment
results.explanation: All findings describe the same rewritten catch block in eventmanager.update that returns `calendarreference?.map(...) ?? []` (and omits console.error), so errors thrown before calendarreference is assigned silently yield an empty result list instead of the previous failure result.

results.title: Webhook secret validation uses non-constant-time string comparison (timing side-channel) and fragile header lookup
distinct_defects: Timing-unsafe webhook secret comparison (non-constant-time !==)
Unhandled req.headers string[]/undefined type causing comparison mismatch
Missing rate limiting on webhook secret verification
Static shared secret as sole authorization without HMAC/timestamp/nonce/per-user scoping
results.explanation: While all findings touch the webhook secret, they include separate root causes with different fixes: timing-safe comparison, header type normalization, rate limiting, and auth design.

results.title: Non-atomic findFirst-then-create in webhook can create duplicate app credentials under concurrent requests
distinct_defects: Non-atomic findFirst-then-create in app-credential.ts allows duplicate credentials under concurrent webhooks due to missing unique constraint on (userId, appId)
results.explanation: All findings describe the same TOCTOU/read-modify-write race in app-credential.ts where a missing unique constraint on (userId, appId) lets concurrent webhooks create duplicate credentials, fixed by a unique constraint with upsert/transaction.

results.title: Webhook API handler performs credential create/update without restricting HTTP method (missing POST-only guard)
distinct_defects: missing HTTP method guard on webhook endpoint
unhandled schema/decryption/JSON parse errors
missing validation of decrypted credential object before persistence
non-constant-time webhook secret comparison
results.explanation: Most findings describe the missing POST/method guard, but the set also includes distinct defects: missing error handling, missing credential-object validation, and timing-unsafe secret comparison.

results.title: Credential-sync token refresh request omits shared secret/Authorization header
distinct_defects: credential-sync endpoint requests are unauthenticated
Lark refresh passes credential-sync flat response to handleLarkError expecting Lark envelope
HubSpot refresh treats raw credential-sync response as HubSpotToken object
Webex refresh loses required token fields from credential-sync response
results.explanation: The findings split into separate defects: missing authentication and provider-specific response-shape mismatches for Lark, HubSpot, and Webex.

results.title: Webhook persists decrypted credential keys without validating per-app credential schema
distinct_defects: missing schema validation of decrypted webhook keys before persisting to credential.key
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the app-credential webhook writes json.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) into credential.key without validating it against the target app's credential schema, differing only in symptoms (silent 200, corruption, downstream parse failures) and line references.

results.title: Webhook updates an arbitrary credential when user has multiple credentials for the same app
distinct_defects: non-atomic find-then-create/upsert race causing duplicate credentials under concurrency
ambiguous credential lookup by userId+appId without a disambiguator causing arbitrary credential overwrite
results.explanation: The findings split into a concurrency/race defect in credential creation and a separate identity/ambiguity defect in credential lookup/update; they require different fixes (atomic upsert/unique constraint vs a disambiguating key).

results.title: Webhook secret header lookup uses raw env header name, breaking auth due to lowercased req.headers keys
distinct_defects: case-normalization of env header name
array-valued duplicate headers
missing-config undefined auth bypass
non-constant-time secret comparison
results.explanation: Most findings share the lowercasing mismatch, but findings 1/2 add duplicate-header array handling, finding 6 adds an undefined-config auth bypass, and finding 4 adds timing-safe comparison as separate defects.

results.title: Webhook auth fails open when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined equals missing header)
distinct_defects: Missing validation that webhook secret is set before comparing request header
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same undefined-comparison authentication bypass caused by an unset Cal.com webhook secret.

results.title: Instance-wide shared webhook secret allows overwriting any user's app credentials (no per-user binding/replay protection)
distinct_defects: Instance-wide static webhook secret authorizes credential writes for arbitrary userid/appslug
No replay/event-identity/version guard permits stale or concurrent credential overwrites
results.explanation: Most findings describe broken authorization scoping via a shared global secret, while others describe missing replay/versioning controls that allow stale or concurrent overwrites; these have different root causes and fixes.

results.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on schema mismatch and can crash calendar operations when callers don’t catch it
distinct_defects: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws instead of returning structured failure, breaking caller branches
credential refresh read-modify-write race clobbers newer tokens
Salesforce refresh-token schema incorrectly requires scope
hardcoded Salesforce login host breaks sandbox orgs
results.explanation: The findings cover four separate root causes: parser error-contract changes, credential-update races, a Salesforce schema error, and a hardcoded login endpoint.

results.title: Webhook credential sync updates key but does not clear previously set invalid flag
distinct_defects: Credential update replaces key but does not reset invalid flag, leaving integration disabled
results.explanation: All three findings describe the same root cause and behavior: updating an existing credential's key without clearing invalid=true leaves the credential disabled after a valid sync.

results.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on Zod safeParse failure, turning previously-graceful token refresh degradation into a hard failure
distinct_defects: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on schema parse failure instead of logging and continuing
results.explanation: All findings describe different symptoms of the same change where parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on schema parse failure rather than logging the Zod error and degrading gracefully.

results.title: Webhook secret check has no rate limiting, enabling unlimited online guessing/brute force
distinct_defects: missing rate limiting on webhook secret check
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same root cause: the webhook endpoint lacks rate limiting, enabling brute-force guessing of the shared secret (finding 0 also adds that this compounds the timing weakness), so a single fix addresses both.

results.title: addGuests input schema allows unbounded guests array (email/DB fan-out DoS vector)
distinct_defects: Missing max/rate limits on guests array enables unbounded guest inserts and email fan-out
addGuests authorization allows any booking attendee (and newly added guests) to add guests instead of organizer/admin
results.explanation: The findings mix an input-size/rate-limit flaw with a separate authorization flaw, so they are not one root cause.

results.title: Authorization bypass: any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking and trigger organizer calendar invites
distinct_defects: Missing booking status/end-time validation allows adding guests to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
Over-permissive attendee-based authorization lets any attendee add arbitrary guests without organizer consent
results.explanation: The findings describe two separate root causes: lack of booking status validation and an authorization flaw that treats any attendee as authorized to add guests.

results.title: add-guests handler emails raw guests list instead of filtered uniqueGuests, causing duplicate/wrong notifications
distinct_defects: sendAddGuestsEmails called with raw guests instead of uniqueguests
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: addguests.handler.ts passes the unfiltered guests input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueguests, causing pre-existing/blacklisted emails to be misclassified and receive the wrong email.

results.title: addGuests crashes with unhandled Prisma P2025 when booking.userId is null (id coerced to 0)
distinct_defects: findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 throws unhandled Prisma P2025 (500) when userId is null
results.explanation: All seven findings describe the same root cause: the `booking.userId || 0` fallback feeding id 0 into findFirstOrThrow, which throws a raw Prisma P2025/500 for bookings with a null userId instead of a handled error.

results.title: Add-guests endpoint can overbook seat-limited events by appending attendees without enforcing seatsPerTimeSlot
distinct_defects: add-guests handler for seated event types lacks seat capacity enforcement and BookingSeat record creation
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the add-guests mutation for seat-based events never validates seat capacity and never creates BookingSeat rows, so seated bookings are overbooked and desynchronized from seat accounting.

results.title: Add-guests email send failure is swallowed (no error context) and request still succeeds
distinct_defects: swallowed sendAddGuestsEmails failure with discarded error and false success response
results.explanation: All eight findings describe the same root cause: the catch around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the error object, logs only a static string, and still returns a success response, so the UI shows 'guests added' even when emails never went out.

results.title: Race condition in addGuests allows duplicate attendee rows (check-then-insert without transaction/unique constraint)
distinct_defects: Non-atomic check-then-insert in addGuests allows duplicate attendees (TOCTOU race / missing unique constraint / no in-flight guard)
results.explanation: All findings describe the same duplicate-attendee race condition in the addGuests flow — a non-atomic dedup check followed by createmany with no transaction, DB uniqueness, or in-flight guard — differing only in which trigger or code location they emphasize.

results.title: Add-guests flow persists new guest attendees with empty name (blank greetings/ICS CN)
distinct_defects: Guest attendees persisted with placeholder identity/timezone data in addguests.handler
results.explanation: All findings trace back to the same root cause: addGuests persists guest attendee rows with an empty name and copied organizer timezone/locale, causing downstream blank-name emails/ICS artifacts and related rendering symptoms.

results.title: Organizer add-guests email sets Reply-To to all attendee emails, leaking roster and risking oversized headers
distinct_defects: unbounded reply-to header including all attendee emails
team-member variant sends organizer-personalized content without teammember prop (email leakage/content mismatch)
results.explanation: Findings 0-5 all describe the same unbounded reply-to header built from all attendees, while finding 6 describes a separate defect where the team-member variant renders organizer-personalized content without the teammember prop.

results.title: Organizer add-guests email subject crashes on empty attendees due to unguarded attendees[0].name access
distinct_defects: unguarded attendees[0].name access in organizer-add-guests-email subject
results.explanation: All findings point to the same line in organizer-add-guests-email.ts using attendees[0].name unguarded, producing either a TypeError on an empty array or an empty guest name in the subject; they are symptoms of one root cause.

results.title: addGuests mutation allows adding guests even when the EventType disables/blocks guests
distinct_defects: addGuests handler fails to enforce event type's disableGuests setting
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the add-guests handler/mutation never checks the event type's guest-disabled restriction, allowing guests when organizers opted out.

results.title: addGuests loads booking by raw id (with heavy includes) before authorization, enabling cross-tenant probing/enumeration
distinct_defects: Unscoped booking lookup before authorization in addguests handler
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the booking is fetched by id without scoping to the requesting user or team before any authorization check, enabling unauthorized access and probing.

results.title: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (//...) as root-relative and rewrites them to the article host
distinct_defects: Incorrect resolution of relative/protocol-relative URLs in absolutizeurls
Incorrect scheme-unaware port handling drops explicit cross-scheme ports
results.explanation: Findings about protocol-relative and document-relative URLs share the same root cause of improper URL resolution, while the port-drop finding is a separate defect with different behavior and fix.

results.title: Embed requests are wrongly rejected due to strict/unnormalized Referer host check (and requiring Referer)
distinct_defects: Referer header trusted as spoofable embeddability/auth gate
Retrieval jobs enqueued before throttle/dedupe, allowing Sidekiq queue flooding
Case-sensitive/unnormalized host comparison against free-form embeddablehost setting
Staff-only throttle bypass in RetrieveTopic job
results.explanation: The findings describe four independent root causes with different fixes: spoofable Referer trust, enqueue-before-throttle/dedupe queue flooding, host normalization/validation mismatch, and staff throttle bypass.

results.title: Unbounded open-uri fetch in TopicEmbed can hang jobs or exhaust Sidekiq memory
distinct_defects: topicembed remote article download lacks open/read timeout and size limit
pollfeed scheduled feed fetch lacks timeout and error handling
results.explanation: The findings describe the same unsafe HTTP pattern but at two different call sites with distinct workers, failure modes, and fixes.

results.title: Destructive `force: true` in create_table migration can drop existing data
distinct_defects: unsafe historical edit to createtoptopics adding force: true
topicembeds migration uses destructive force: true and lacks foreign keys/dependent cleanup
results.explanation: Findings 0-3 and 5-7 all concern the already-shipped toptopics migration being destructively edited, while finding 4 concerns a separate topicembeds migration with its own force: true and schema/cleanup issues.

results.title: Redis throttle key can become permanent due to non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE
distinct_defects: non-atomic setnx+expire leaves throttle key without TTL
results.explanation: All findings describe the same non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE race in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? that can leave a permanent TTL-less throttle key, fixed by a single atomic SET NX EX.

results.title: Redirect-based SSRF: only initial URL host is validated while open-uri follows redirects
distinct_defects: SSRF via open-uri redirects not revalidated against allowed host
Missing scheme validation in TopicEmbed#import_remote allowing SSRF/pipe-to-shell
results.explanation: Findings 0-6 share the same redirect-revalidation root cause, while finding 7 describes a separate lack of scheme validation before open(url).

results.title: TopicEmbed re-import crashes when the embedded post was deleted (embed.post is nil)
distinct_defects: TopicEmbed rows lack dependent-destroy cleanup when their topic or post is deleted, leaving stale topicid/nil post references
results.explanation: All findings are symptoms of the same root cause: TopicEmbed has no lifecycle cleanup on topic/post deletion, so deleted imports leave orphaned rows with stale topicids or nil posts that break embed rendering and re-import.

results.title: Race condition: non-atomic exists?/create! on TopicEmbed causes RecordNotUnique under concurrent imports
distinct_defects: check-then-create race on unique TopicEmbed embedurl
enqueue/publish before outer transaction commits
results.explanation: Findings 0-2 and 4-7 describe the same TOCTOU race on the unique embedurl index, while finding 3 describes a separate transactional visibility defect where async consumers see uncommitted or missing topics.

results.title: Embed URL lookup uses exact, unnormalized string match, allowing duplicate topics for equivalent URLs
distinct_defects: embedurl identity/join key lacks canonicalization, causing duplicate topics and mismatched lookups
results.explanation: Every finding attributes the duplicate/mismatched topic behavior to the same root cause: the raw embedurl string is used as the article identity and join key without URL normalization across all producers and lookups.

results.title: Unrescued inline feed poll aborts HTTP fallback on embed cache miss
distinct_defects: Inline feed poll exceptions abort performretrieve before HTTP fallback and may propagate into retry logic
Every embed cache miss runs a full synchronous feed poll, repeatedly downloading/importing the entire feed per URL
results.explanation: The findings describe two separate defects: missing error isolation around the feed poll, and unconditional per-cache-miss full feed polling causing work amplification.

results.title: TopicEmbed advances contentsha1 even when post revision fails, permanently skipping future re-syncs
distinct_defects: ignored revise! failure with unconditional contentsha1 advance
missing update-path spec coverage/nil-post edge
concurrent import body/digest race
results.explanation: Most findings share the same ignored revise! result defect, but the spec/nil-post gap and the concurrent import race are separate root causes.

results.title: TopicEmbed embedurl column defaults to varchar(255), causing failures for valid long URLs during imports/polling
distinct_defects: embedurl varchar(255) too short for long URLs
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the embedurl column is limited to varchar(255), so longer feed/article URLs fail during insert in the import transaction.

results.title: Throttle key is acquired before successful fetch and uses non-atomic setnx+expire, causing skipped retries or permanent lockout
distinct_defects: Premature throttle key set before fetch success suppresses retries
Non-atomic setnx plus expire can leave permanent throttle key
results.explanation: Most findings describe setting the deduplication key before retrieval succeeds, but findings 3 and 6 describe a separate atomicity bug where a crash between setnx and expire leaves the key without a TTL.

results.title: TopicEmbed import mutates caller-owned contents via `<<`, causing duplicate footers and FrozenError on frozen strings
distinct_defects: mutating caller-owned contents string with <<
contentsha1 hashes locale-dependent imported-from footer
results.explanation: Most findings describe in-place mutation of the caller's string, but finding 3 describes a separate hash-instability defect where contentsha1 includes the translated footer and can change with locale/translation updates.

results.title: Existing TopicEmbed updates ignore title-only changes, leaving topic titles stale
distinct_defects: update branch ignores title, only revises post body
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the existing-embed update path in topicembed.rb gates only on the body digest and never writes the article title, leaving the topic title stale after retitling.

results.title: TopicEmbed URL guard uses line-anchored regex and later calls URI() without rescue, allowing malformed/multiline URLs to crash imports
distinct_defects: TopicEmbedImport mutates caller's contents string in place
line-anchored URL scheme regex allows multiline bypass/injection
unhandled URI parse errors abort import on malformed or degenerate URLs
EmbedController rescues wrong URI exception for invalid referer bytes
results.explanation: The findings cover four separate root causes: a caller-string mutation, a line-anchor regex bypass, unhandled malformed-URL parsing in the import path, and mismatched referer URI exception handling.

results.title: Embed/topic retrieval synchronously runs full feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed) on cache miss, coupling embeds to feed health and enabling resource exhaustion
distinct_defects: performretrieve synchronously runs the full pollfeed job inline with no error isolation before fetchhttp
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: TopicRetriever#performRetrieve calls jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inline on the embed-request path without error isolation, producing varying symptoms (exception propagation aborting fetchhttp, unauthenticated resource amplification, broken-feed coupling).

results.title: TopicEmbed uses open(url) without requiring open-uri, causing URL opens to be treated as local files
distinct_defects: missing require 'open-uri' before open(url) in app/models/topicembed.rb
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: TopicEmbed#import_remote calls open(url) without requiring 'open-uri', so Kernel#open falls back to file semantics and raises Errno::ENOENT.

results.title: Embed topic retrieval can crash or silently no-op when embedbyusername is blank/missing, leaving embeds stuck on infinite “loading”
distinct_defects: Nil/blank embedbyusername raises NoMethodError on downcase
Missing/mismatched configured user silently returns and leaves embed loading
results.explanation: The findings split between a line-49 crash when the setting is nil and a line-50 silent no-op when no user matches, which are distinct failure modes with different fixes.

results.title: Gemfile updated with new gems but default Gemfile.lock not regenerated, breaking frozen/deployment bundler installs
distinct_defects: Gemfile additions not reflected in default gemfile.lock (only gemfilerails4.lock regenerated)
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: ruby-readability and simple-rss added to the Gemfile while only gemfilerails4.lock was regenerated, leaving the default gemfile.lock stale and breaking frozen/deployment bundle installs.

results.title: Redis throttle key is set before retrieval succeeds, suppressing retries after failures
distinct_defects: throttle key set before retrieval succeeds and never cleared on failure
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: retrieved_recently? commits the 60-second Redis throttle key via setnx before perform_retrieve runs and never releases it on failure, suppressing legitimate retries.

results.title: Embeddable host validation uses strict string equality, rejecting valid hosts with different casing or with a scheme included
distinct_defects: case-sensitive hostname comparison
configured host contains scheme causing exact host mismatch
results.explanation: Findings 0-2 share case-sensitive hostname comparison, while finding 3 is a separate exact-equality mismatch caused by entering a scheme in the configured host.

results.title: Migration backfills posts.cookmethod to rawhtml, causing all existing posts to bypass cooking/sanitization
distinct_defects: migration default cook_method assigns rawhtml enum to existing posts
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same migration defaulting posts to the raw HTML enum value, causing historical posts to bypass cooking.

results.title: Dead feed-modified cache key means PollFeed always re-downloads and reprocesses the full feed
distinct_defects: unused feedkey dead code enabling full re-downloads
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the feedkey cache key is defined but never used, so the hourly poll re-downloads and re-imports the entire feed instead of leveraging modification caching.

distinct_defects: incorrect default-port comparison in absolutize_urls
protocol-relative URLs treated as root-relative
results.explanation: The findings identify two separate root causes in URL absolutization: port logic compares against the wrong default port, while protocol-relative URLs are misclassified by a leading-slash check and rewritten incorrectly.

results.title: Poll feed processing calls `String#scrub` via `stringscrub`, crashing on Ruby 2.0 (requires Ruby >= 2.1)
distinct_defects: String#scrub unavailable on Ruby 2.0
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1+, but the project runs on Ruby 2.0, causing NomethodError on feed polling.

results.title: Embed source hash includes localized footer, causing false-positive content changes on locale/footer updates
distinct_defects: content hash includes localized footer, coupling change detection to presentation text
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same root cause: the SHA1 change-detection hash is computed over the locale-translated footer, so presentation/locale changes spuriously trigger post revisions.

results.title: `skip_validations` allows saving posts/topics with invalid or unsafe data (validations fully bypassed)
distinct_defects: skipvalidations bypasses ActiveRecord validations
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same root cause: the new skipvalidations option lets callers persist invalid posts/topics without validation, with the nil/blank title being one concrete symptom.

results.title: TopicEmbed import uses non-atomic exists?/create! allowing concurrent duplicates and unhandled RecordNotUnique
distinct_defects: topicembed.rb import check-then-create race
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same check-then-create race in topicembed.rb's import, where concurrent imports of the same URL pass the exists? check and the loser fails on the unique index, causing duplicate topics, unhandled RecordNotUnique, and leaving orphaned state.

results.title: RetrieveTopic job unnecessarily eager-loads mail stack via stray require_dependency
distinct_defects: unused require 'email/sender' in retrievetopic.rb
results.explanation: Both findings describe the same copy-pasted, unused 'email/sender' require in app/jobs/regular/retrievetopic.rb, one noting it is unused and the other that it needlessly eager-loads the mail stack.

results.title: Admin::GroupsController#add_members splits usernames without trimming, causing spaced names to be skipped while still returning success
distinct_defects: addMembers silently skips unmatched or whitespace-padded usernames while returning successJSON
results.explanation: All findings describe the same addMembers input-handling defect: comma-split usernames are not trimmed and unresolved names are silently dropped, so partial or empty additions still report success.

results.title: Admin group creation drops submitted aliaslevel and saves default instead
distinct_defects: Group create action drops aliaslevel parameter
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: the admin groups create action only assigns name/visible and never persists the client-submitted aliaslevel, so newly created groups silently fall back to the default alias level.

results.title: PATCH updates unintentionally hide groups when `visible` param is omitted (and legacy membership changes are ignored)
distinct_defects: Breaking admin Groups API contract: nested group[...] params removed and updatepatch deleted without deprecation
Incorrect visible assignment on create/update: unconditional and strict string comparison cause silent false
results.explanation: The findings split into two independent root causes: an API contract/backward-compatibility break and a faulty visible-parameter assignment.

results.title: Admin::GroupsController specs hardcode group id=1, implicitly depending on seeded automatic group
distinct_defects: Hardcoded id/groupid 1 relying on seeded automatic group instead of fabricate(:group, automatic: true)
results.explanation: All findings describe the same root cause: specs hardcode id: 1 / groupid: 1 and depend on Discourse seed data providing an automatic group rather than creating one via fabricate(:group, automatic: true), with the same fix.

results.title: Group name is stripped on create but not on update, allowing whitespace-padded names
distinct_defects: group name not stripped in update path
results.explanation: All four findings describe the same root cause: the update action assigns params[:name] without the .strip normalization that create applies, so the fix is shared.
